These findings were consistent with interstitial nephritis.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 42-year-old man presented to the ED after being attacked by Asian giant hornets, sustaining approximately 66 sting marks. Initial symptoms included difficulty breathing, headache, numbness, and oliguria (200 ml/24h). On day 3, laboratory tests showed elevated CK (5342.3 U/L), AST (1124.00 U/L), and serum creatinine (185.00 umol/L), indicating rhabdomyolysis and acute kidney injury. Ten days later, oliguria persisted, and serum creatinine rose to 534 umol/L. By day 17, renal function further deteriorated with oliguria (250 ml/24h) and serum creatinine peaking at 1130.5 umol/L. A kidney biopsy performed on day 17 revealed interstitial inflammation with edema, focal infiltration of eosinophils and lymphocytes, and normal glomeruli, consistent with interstitial nephritis. The patient was treated with oral methylprednisolone 32 mg/day. By day 31, his urine output increased to over 2.8 L/day, and serum creatinine decreased to 159.3 umol/L, indicating a positive response to treatment.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with acute kidney injury following hornet stings, characterized by oliguria and elevated creatinine.
Initial injury involved rhabdomyolysis, indicated by significantly elevated creatine kinase and aspartate aminotransferase.
Kidney function progressively worsened, with creatinine peaking at 1130.5 umol/L and persistent oliguria.
Kidney biopsy confirmed interstitial nephritis, showing interstitial inflammation with eosinophils and lymphocytes, and normal glomeruli.
Renal ultrasound on day 17 showed increased kidney size and parenchyma thickness, consistent with acute kidney injury.
Treatment with methylprednisolone led to improved urine output and a significant decrease in serum creatinine.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.alternative: Acute tubular necrosis (ATN) as the sole cause of AKI
ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: While rhabdomyolysis can cause ATN, the biopsy specifically identified interstitial nephritis (E006), and the presence of eosinophils and lymphocytes points away from pure ATN.
